learning_goal: Name the derivative of each of the four pharyngeal pouches from its dorsal and ventral wings, explain by the descent of the thymus why the inferior parathyroids come from a higher pouch than the superior ones, and use that to predict the findings in DiGeorge syndrome and to locate an ectopic parathyroid gland.

structures.name: Pharyngeal endoderm — the lateral wall of the pharynx
structures.label: Pharyngeal endoderm — the lateral wall of the pharynx
structures.narration: The wall the pouches come out of, and the reason they are endodermal. Everything a pouch becomes is made of this: endoderm makes epithelium and glands, so every pouch derivative is either a lined cavity or a gland. It is cut away on the right in the first view so you can look at the left wall from inside the lumen, which is where the pouches open.

structures.name: The pharyngeal arches — the bars the pouches lie between
structures.label: The pharyngeal arches — the bars the pouches lie between
structures.narration: The arches are bars of mesenchyme, and they are here only as the thing the pouches lie between. Their cartilages, muscles, cranial nerves and arch arteries belong to the Pharyngeal arches entry and are deliberately absent. What matters here is the geography: a pouch sits in the gap between two bars, and the cleft for that same gap sits on the other side of them.

structures.name: Surface ectoderm — the body surface
structures.label: Surface ectoderm — the body surface
structures.narration: The outside of the neck — the ectoderm the clefts are grooves IN. It is drawn here because a groove is a feature of a surface, and until this surface existed the four clefts were four crescents hanging in space with nothing to be a groove in. It is shown only in the sectioned view, and faintly: it encloses everything else, so a beat that stands outside it would be looking at skin. What a student should take from it is the arrangement — pharyngeal endoderm on the inside, this on the outside, arch mesenchyme between, and the two epithelia meeting at four levels with only a membrane between them. The second arch then overgrows the lower three grooves into a cervical sinus which normally obliterates; where it does not, the remnant is a branchial cyst on the side of the neck.

structures.name: The FIRST cleft — ECTODERM, on the outside
structures.label: The FIRST cleft — ECTODERM, on the outside
structures.narration: A groove on the OUTSIDE, lined by ectoderm, and drawn in a colour nothing on the inside of the apparatus uses for exactly one reason: the single commonest error in this topic is attributing a cleft derivative to a pouch. Keep the two sides apart from the first sentence and nothing later gets mixed up. This is the cleft that matters most — it persists as the external acoustic meatus, and where it meets the first pouch it builds the tympanic membrane.

structures.name: The second, third and fourth clefts — buried by the cervical sinus
structures.label: The second, third and fourth clefts — buried by the cervical sinus
structures.narration: The same germ layer and the same side of the apparatus as the first cleft — the shade is darker only so a beat can point at one group without pointing at the other. These three are overgrown by the second arch and buried as the cervical sinus, which normally disappears. What happens when it does not is the Pharyngeal clefts and membranes entry, not this one.

structures.name: The median plane
structures.label: The median plane
structures.narration: A reference, not a structure. Everything in this scene is a PAIR — four pairs of pouches, two parathyroid pairs, two thymic strands — and the one thing that crosses this plane is the thymus, whose two strands meet on it. The rod stops above the thymus on purpose, so it does not sit in front of the fusion it exists to let you judge.

structures.name: Pouch 1 — the middle ear and the auditory tube
structures.label: Pouch 1 — the middle ear and the auditory tube
structures.narration: The first pouch elongates into the tubotympanic recess. Its far end expands into the middle ear cavity and the mastoid antrum, and its narrow proximal part stays as the auditory tube — which is why the middle ear is, embryologically, a blind end of the pharynx and why infection climbs that tube so easily in children. Where the pouch meets the first cleft from outside, endoderm and ectoderm come together with a thin layer of mesoderm between them, and that three-layered sheet is the tympanic membrane.

structures.name: Pouch 2 — the palatine tonsil
structures.label: Pouch 2 — the palatine tonsil
structures.narration: The second pouch is largely obliterated as the palatine tonsil grows into it. The endoderm gives the surface epithelium and the lining of the tonsillar crypts; the lymphoid tissue itself infiltrates later from the surrounding mesenchyme. What is left of the pouch is the tonsillar fossa the tonsil sits in.

structures.name: Pouch 3 — thymus below, inferior parathyroid above
structures.label: Pouch 3 — thymus below, inferior parathyroid above
structures.narration: The third pouch is the important one. Its ventral wing becomes the thymus and its dorsal wing becomes the inferior parathyroid gland. Both then travel: the thymus migrates down and medially into the anterior mediastinum, and the inferior parathyroid is dragged along with it for part of the way before separating. Hold on to the fact that the inferior parathyroid comes from the third pouch, because the next region contradicts what the names suggest.

structures.name: Pouch 4 — superior parathyroid, and the C cells
structures.label: Pouch 4 — superior parathyroid, and the C cells
structures.narration: The fourth pouch gives the superior parathyroid gland from its dorsal wing and the ultimopharyngeal body from its ventral wing. The ultimopharyngeal body is absorbed into the thyroid and disperses as the parafollicular or C cells that secrete calcitonin — and note that the C cells themselves are neural crest cells that came in through the pouch, not endoderm. Some texts describe a small fifth pouch as the source of the ultimopharyngeal body; treat it as part of the fourth and the answer is the same.

structures.name: Third pouch, DORSAL wing — the inferior parathyroid
structures.label: Third pouch, DORSAL wing — the inferior parathyroid
structures.narration: The dorsal wing of the third pouch, which becomes the inferior parathyroid gland. Dorsal wings make parathyroid tissue in BOTH pouches — that is the half of the pattern worth holding on to, because it means the only thing you have to remember separately is what the two ventral wings do.

structures.name: Third pouch, VENTRAL wing — the thymus
structures.label: Third pouch, VENTRAL wing — the thymus
structures.narration: The ventral wing of the third pouch, which becomes the thymus. It is the wing that travels, and everything counter-intuitive in this topic follows from how far it goes.

structures.name: Fourth pouch, DORSAL wing — the superior parathyroid
structures.label: Fourth pouch, DORSAL wing — the superior parathyroid
structures.narration: The dorsal wing of the fourth pouch, which becomes the superior parathyroid gland. Same rule as the third: dorsal wing, parathyroid tissue. This one barely moves from where it starts.

structures.name: Fourth pouch, VENTRAL wing — the ultimopharyngeal body
structures.label: Fourth pouch, VENTRAL wing — the ultimopharyngeal body
structures.narration: The ventral wing of the fourth pouch, which becomes the ultimopharyngeal body. Some texts credit a small fifth pouch with it instead; treat it as part of the fourth and the answer is the same.

structures.name: The tympanic membrane — three layers, two germ layers meeting
structures.label: The tympanic membrane — three layers, two germ layers meeting
structures.narration: Where the first pouch meets the first cleft from outside, endoderm and ectoderm come together with a thin layer of mesoderm between them, and that three-layered sheet is the tympanic membrane. It is the one place in this scene where a pouch and a cleft touch, which is why it is drawn between them and in neither of their two colours.

structures.name: The palatine tonsil, filling the second pouch
structures.label: The palatine tonsil, filling the second pouch
structures.narration: The tonsil grows INTO the second pouch and largely obliterates it, which is why the two are drawn sharing space here rather than side by side. The endoderm gives the surface epithelium and the crypt lining; the lymphoid tissue infiltrates later from the surrounding mesenchyme. What is left of the pouch is the fossa the tonsil sits in.

structures.name: The thymus — the organ that travels furthest
structures.label: The thymus — the organ that travels furthest
structures.narration: Two strands from the two third pouches, growing caudally and medially until they meet on the median plane behind the sternum. Watch how far it goes, because the distance is the mechanism: the thymus is what drags the third pouch parathyroid past the fourth pouch one.

structures.name: The ultimopharyngeal body, on its way into the thyroid
structures.label: The ultimopharyngeal body, on its way into the thyroid
structures.narration: The ventral wing of the fourth pouch, travelling into the thyroid, where it is absorbed and disperses. It is present in the middle of this process and gone by the end — which is the whole of its story, and the reason the C cells end up somewhere the fourth pouch never reaches.

structures.name: The parafollicular (C) cells, dispersed through the thyroid
structures.label: The parafollicular (C) cells, dispersed through the thyroid
structures.narration: What the ultimopharyngeal body becomes: cells scattered through the thyroid rather than a lump in it, which is why they are drawn as a scatter. They arrive through the fourth pouch but they are neural crest in origin, and that one fact is what makes medullary thyroid carcinoma behave the way it does.

structures.name: The thymopharyngeal duct — the route, and where things get left behind
structures.label: The thymopharyngeal duct — the route, and where things get left behind
structures.narration: The trail the descending thymus draws out behind it, from the third pouch to the mediastinum. It normally disappears. Where it does not, it is a cervical thymic cyst — and because the inferior parathyroid is towed along this same line, every ectopic site that gland can occupy lies somewhere on it. This is the structure to look at when you are asked where a missing adenoma is.

structures.name: The INFERIOR parathyroid — from the THIRD pouch
structures.label: The INFERIOR parathyroid — from the THIRD pouch
structures.narration: From the third pouch, and it ends up BELOW the gland that came from the fourth. Follow it rather than memorising it: it starts above its neighbour, it is towed down past it, and it stops at the lower pole of the thyroid. Because it was towed rather than placed, its final position is far more variable than the superior gland’s, and that is the surgical consequence.

structures.name: The SUPERIOR parathyroid — from the FOURTH pouch
structures.label: The SUPERIOR parathyroid — from the FOURTH pouch
structures.narration: From the fourth pouch, and it hardly moves at all: it stays at the level it started and ends up on the upper-posterior surface of the thyroid. It is the gland that is where you expect it, and it is the reference against which the inferior gland’s journey is measured.

structures.name: The thyroid gland — the landmark both parathyroids end up on
structures.label: The thyroid gland — the landmark both parathyroids end up on
structures.narration: Context, and a landmark. Thyroid development is a different entry — the foramen caecum, the thyroglossal duct and the ectopic thyroid are not taught here. What it is doing in this scene is carrying the two levels the parathyroids come to rest at: the superior gland at its upper pole, the inferior gland at its lower pole. That is the crossover, drawn on one gland.

views.title: Look at the apparatus from the inside
views.narration:
Turn the embryo inside out and look at the wall of the pharynx from the lumen. Between the arches, the endoderm pockets outwards four times on each side. These are the pouches. Everything they make is endodermal — a lined cavity or a gland — and everything the clefts make outside is ectodermal. Keep those two sides apart from the first sentence and nothing later gets mixed up.

Get the geography right before any list. The arches are bars, the clefts are grooves on the outside lined by ectoderm, and the pouches are the matching pockets on the inside lined by endoderm. Four pairs of pouches count. Endoderm makes epithelium and glands, so almost everything a pouch becomes is either a glandular organ or a lined cavity.

views.title: Split each pouch into its two wings

the dorsal wing of the fourth pouch gives
the ventral wing of the fourth pouch gives

views.narration:
Cut across and notice that the third and fourth pouches are not single pockets. Each has a dorsal and a ventral wing, and each wing has its own fate. Both dorsal wings make parathyroid tissue. The ventral wing of the third makes the thymus; the ventral wing of the fourth makes the ultimopharyngeal body. Two pouches, four organs, and the pattern is symmetrical enough to reconstruct under pressure.

The third and fourth pouches each split into a dorsal wing and a ventral wing, and each wing makes a different organ. This is the detail that turns a memorised list into something you can reconstruct. Dorsal wings make parathyroid tissue in both pouches. The ventral wing of the third makes the thymus, and the ventral wing of the fourth makes the ultimopharyngeal body.

views.title: Down the series: ear, tonsil, thymus, parathyroid
views.narration: Run down the four pouches. One becomes the tubotympanic recess — middle ear, mastoid antrum and auditory tube — and meets the first cleft to build the tympanic membrane. Two is filled in by the palatine tonsil and leaves the tonsillar fossa. Three gives the thymus and the inferior parathyroid. Four gives the superior parathyroid and the ultimopharyngeal body, whose cells become the calcitonin-secreting C cells of the thyroid.

views.title: The trail the thymus leaves
views.narration:
The thymic primordia grow caudally as two strands, meet in the midline and settle behind the sternum in the anterior mediastinum. Any part of the strand left behind stays where it stopped, which is why ectopic thymic tissue and thymic cysts turn up anywhere along a line from the angle of the mandible to the sternum. The thymus keeps growing until puberty and then involutes into fat, and an absent thymic shadow on a neonatal chest film is a real clue to a pouch failure.

Because the inferior gland travels with the thymus, it can stop anywhere along that route or overshoot it. An inferior parathyroid may sit high in the neck, inside the carotid sheath, inside the thymus, or down in the anterior mediastinum. That is why an adenoma is not always found at the first neck exploration and why the mediastinum is searched when hyperparathyroidism persists after surgery. The superior gland, which barely moved, is where you expect it.

views.title: The thymus descends and the parathyroids cross
views.narration:
Now watch the movement, because it is the movement that produces the exam question. The thymus grows down towards the anterior mediastinum and tows the third pouch parathyroid behind it, past the fourth pouch parathyroid which barely moves. The result is a crossover: inferior parathyroids from the third pouch, superior parathyroids from the fourth. Because the inferior gland was towed, it can stop anywhere along the route — high in the neck, in the carotid sheath, inside the thymus or in the mediastinum — and that is where a missing adenoma hides.

Here is the point the examiner is testing. Parathyroid tissue from the third pouch ends up below parathyroid tissue from the fourth, so the inferior glands come from the higher pouch and the superior glands from the lower one. The reason is the thymus: it descends a long way and drags the third pouch parathyroid past the fourth pouch parathyroid on the way. Because it is towed rather than placed, the inferior gland's final position is far more variable than the superior gland's — the surgical consequence follows directly.

views.title: The ultimopharyngeal body becomes the C cells

ops.kind: is absorbed into the thyroid and disperses as

views.narration: The C cells arrive through the fourth pouch but they are neural crest in origin, and that single fact explains the tumour they give rise to. Medullary thyroid carcinoma is not a follicular cell tumour: it does not concentrate iodine, so radioiodine does not treat it, it is followed with serum calcitonin instead of thyroglobulin, and it belongs with phaeochromocytoma in the multiple endocrine neoplasia type two syndromes through the RET gene. A thyroid cancer that behaves like a neuroendocrine tumour makes sense once you know where its cells came from.

views.title: When the pouches do not form
views.narration:
Take away the third and fourth pouches and you have written the case yourself. No thymus, so a baby with recurrent viral and fungal infection and no thymic shadow on the film. No parathyroids, so hypocalcaemia presenting as tetany or a neonatal seizure. The same neural crest cells build the cardiac outflow tract, so add truncus arteriosus or an interrupted aortic arch, with cleft palate and abnormal facies. That is DiGeorge, and it is one deletion producing four systems' worth of findings. Finish with the four-line summary and the crossover, and the topic is closed.

One deletion, one set of cells, and you can predict the whole picture. Neural crest cells fail to populate the third and fourth pouch territory, so the thymus and the parathyroids do not form. No thymus means no T cell maturation and a baby with recurrent viral and fungal infection. No parathyroids means hypocalcaemia, and the presentation is often neonatal tetany or a seizure in the first days of life. The same cells build the outflow tract of the heart, so add a conotruncal defect — truncus arteriosus or an interrupted aortic arch. Cleft palate and abnormal facies complete it. Two practical points: no live vaccines, and irradiate any blood products.

The queue carries it as `built` for the review task.

EVERY STRUCTURE BUILDS GEOMETRY AT t = 1 AND SOME OF THEM ARE VESTIGES THERE. This is a workaround for queue item 137 (engine__procedural-ref-default-t), not an anatomical claim. viz3d.js parseProceduralRef (:478) defaults an unpinned ref to t = 1 at mount; a structure that builds nothing at t = 1 comes back reason:"none", never enters meshes[], and restage() (:1854) filters on `meshes[s.key] && adapter.stageable(s)` — so SET_STAGE can never bring it back at any later t. Two independent reviews have converged on fix (a) for that item and it is not a scene’s to make. So the pouch stems, the four wings, the thymopharyngeal duct and the ultimopharyngeal body never shrink below a tenth of their peak size. NO BEAT SHOWS ONE OF THEM AT A t WHERE IT IS A VESTIGE: the wings appear only in beat 2 (day 38, their peak), the ultimopharyngeal body only in beat 7 (day 48, at 0.50 of its peak — corrected by the review task 2026-10-03: this said “day 44, its peak” and beat 7 stands at day 48, where the model's own B7-body claim measures the body at 0.50 of peak; the substantive claim that no beat shows a structure at its mounting floor is unaffected and the harness proves it independently), and the pouch stems only up to beat 3. Acceptance row V measures every one of them at peak against t = 1 and requires at least a fourfold collapse, so a reviewer can see which structures the floor applies to and that it is a floor rather than a drawn shape. The second pouch is deliberately NOT on that list: what is left of it at t = 1 is the tonsillar fossa, which is real, so it is floored at 0.38 of its peak as anatomy and not at the mounting vestige.

NO NARRATION CLAIM IN THIS SCENE NAMES A SIDE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. RENDER-STANDARD: "A model with no chiral content cannot witness its own handedness, and an acceptance test written in the same coordinates as the declaration is circular, however carefully it is floored." Every structure here is built as a mirror-symmetric PAIR about x = 0 — which is what "four pairs of pouches count" means — so flipping the sign of x in the model’s AXES declaration would leave every acceptance row passing and change nothing a student could see. Acceptance row Y asserts the symmetry the model does have; it does not assert handedness. Any future claim here about a LEFT or RIGHT pouch, gland or strand is UNPROVEN until the model carries a landmark that is independently right/left determined, or a corpus-level test checks its axes string against a mesh-anchored model.

THE FIFTH POUCH is described as rudimentary and treated as part of the fourth, which is how most texts present it. Where a text counts it separately it is credited with the ultimopharyngeal body — the derivative is the same either way, and the narration says so rather than picking a side. No separate geometry is built for it.

WHETHER THE C CELLS ARE ENDODERMAL OR NEURAL CREST is not universally stated the same way across texts. The scene teaches the neural crest origin because that is what makes medullary thyroid carcinoma and its behaviour make sense, and it says so explicitly rather than leaving it implied. The geometry cannot express a cell’s lineage: the C cells are drawn in a colour of their own inside the thyroid, and the claim is carried by the words.

THE AUDITORY TUBE AND THE MIDDLE EAR CAVITY ARE NOT SEPARATE KEYS. They are the two ends of ONE solid, pouch1, whose calibre is narrow where it leaves the pharynx and expanded at its far end. There is no waist between them — it is a continuous taper — and RENDER-STANDARD says segment boundaries belong at the waists, so a key boundary there would draw a border a student would then look for in a specimen. The consequence is that a beat cannot highlight the tube alone. What beat 4 does instead is measure the calibre ratio off the built recess (acceptance row E1-calibre, 3.51 at t = 1 against a floor of 1.8) and name both parts in the narration.
THE MASTOID ANTRUM is inside the pouch-1 expansion and is not separately drawn, for the same reason. It is named in the narration and in match.terms.

THE DESCENT IS DRIVEN BY DIFFERENTIAL GROWTH, which is the mechanism, but the model does not build the structures that do the growing — there is no neck, no sternum, no mediastinum and no great vessels here. The thymus’s resting place is expressed as a stated number of intersegments below the thyroid’s lower pole and ventral of the pharyngeal axis, which is "retrosternal" in this frame without a sternum in it. A student looking for the sternum will not find it.

WEEK NUMBERS ARE THE STANDARD TEACHING APPROXIMATIONS. t = 0 is day 22 and t = 1 is day 56; pouches bud through weeks four and five and thymic descent is complete by about week eight. Texts differ by several days and the narration gives them as approximations. The crown-rump length law the whole model scales by is a least-squares fit through three stated anchors (2.0 mm at day 22, 8.0 mm at day 35, 30.0 mm at day 56) with a real residual — reported by acceptance row G-fit as rms 0.157 in ln(mm), i.e. about 17%. That is the accuracy of the sizes in this scene.

THE SOLVED CROSSOVER DAY IS 41.6, and it is a property of this model rather than a datum from a text. What is anatomically load-bearing is the ORDER — that the pouch-3 gland ends below the pouch-4 one — and the day is what falls out of the descent geometry when you ask when the sign flips. Texts do not give a day for the crossover. Beat 6 claims it only as "the second half of the descent" (between day 36 and 48), which is as much as the model can honestly support.

"Pharyngeal arches" is NOT claimed in covers[]. The arches are built as context — the bars the pouches lie between — and the arch cartilages, muscles, cranial nerves and arch arteries belong to that entry and are deliberately absent here.

"Pharyngeal clefts & membranes" is NOT claimed. The clefts are built because the first one is needed for the tympanic membrane and because keeping ectoderm visibly apart from endoderm is this topic’s commonest error — but the external acoustic meatus, the cervical sinus, the branchial cyst and the branchial fistula belong to that entry.

"Thyroid gland development" is NOT claimed. The thyroid is built as context and as the landmark both parathyroid pairs come to rest on; the ultimopharyngeal body is followed only as far as the C cells joining it. The descent from the foramen caecum, the thyroglossal duct and the ectopic thyroid are that entry’s subject.

IMMUNOLOGY BEYOND THE CONSEQUENCE OF AN ABSENT THYMUS is not taught here. T cell development, thymic selection and the full immunodeficiency differential belong to physiology and immunology; this scene names only the clinical picture that follows from the pouch failing.

THE PARATHYROID GLANDS’ PHYSIOLOGY — parathyroid hormone, calcium regulation, primary and secondary hyperparathyroidism — is named only where it explains the surgical relevance of an ectopic gland. It appears in match.terms so a highlighted term still reaches this scene.

VIEW MODES. CURRICULUM.json asks this structure for `cross_section` and `glands`, and both are supplied: beats 1 and 4 are cross_section, beats 3 and 7 are glands. The eight beats of the 3D scene replace the five of the sequence scene — three new views were authored because three of the original beats were carrying two pictures each: the descent and the trail it leaves are not the same frame (beats 5 and 6), the ear is not the same frame as the run down the series (beat 4), and the C cells are not the same frame as the fourth pouch (beat 7).

THE TWO OPS THE SVG SCENE AUTHORED THAT ARE NOT CARRIED OVER. PEEL_LAYER on the organ layer was authored in the old beat 5 because the same flat panel was read twice, once for what forms and once for what is missing; in 3D that is two cameras on two stages and the work is done by beat 6 and beat 8 standing at the SAME day and the SAME anterior camera with three structures hidden, which is a true with-and-without pair rather than a degraded op. TRACE_STRUCTURE on concept:pouch-series and concept:thymic-descent is not carried over either: the procedural adapter degrades TRACE to a highlight (viz3d.js:536) because a procedural model has no centreline to walk, and both traces were pointing at concepts rather than at drawn regions in any case. What they were for — progression through the series, migration over time — is now carried by SET_STAGE and by the beats being at different days.

CROSS_SECTION CUTS ONLY THE CONTEXT STRUCTURES, and beat 1 depends on that. viz3d.js:2438 sets `m.material.clippingPlanes = (clipping && !isTaught(s)) ? [clipPlane] : null`, and isTaught is true for any role other than "context" (viz3d.js:167). So beat 1’s CROSS_SECTION on x opens the pharyngeal wall — which is role "context" for exactly this reason — and leaves the pouches whole, which is the dissection the narration asks for: look at the wall of the pharynx from the lumen. If a later edit promotes pharyngeal_wall to a taught role, beat 1 stops being a cutaway and becomes an outside view of an opaque tube.

THE CROSS_SECTION OFFSET IS 0 AND MUST STAY 0. The player multiplies the authored offset by 3 (viz3d.js:2061) and applies the plane in WORLD space, after fit() has normalised the scene; the model’s own units change with t because the whole apparatus scales with crown-rump length. An offset of 0 is the median plane at every t and under any normalisation. A non-zero offset in this scene would mean a different anatomical level at every beat, which is why the old beat 2’s `CROSS_SECTION axis y offset 0` was dropped rather than retargeted: on this model a y-cut at the world origin is above everything and removes nothing.

THE LATERAL LAYOUT WAS REBUILT 2026-10-03 FROM REVIEW FINDINGS F1 AND F4, AND THE APPOSITION IS NOW EXACT BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN MEASURED AND HOPED FOR. The old layout placed all four grooves at one stated radius (F_CLEFT = 3.60 intersegments) chosen by eye; measured, the first pouch stopped 1.93 intersegments short of the first cleft at EVERY t, with the tympanic membrane floating in the middle of that void touching neither. Now: a groove's floor is placed on its own pouch's end tangent one membrane-thickness beyond its dome, so pouch-to-cleft is F_MEMB by construction (0.1019 of an intersegment measured at day 44); the body surface is SOLVED to pass through the grooves' lips; and the other three grooves' depths are derived from that surface. Claims B1-appose, B1-groove, B4-apart, B4-not-fused, B4-touches and B4-touches-pouch assert all of it at the beats' own t, and acceptance rows AP and AG assert it across six days.

surface_ectoderm IS NEW AND IS A SHELL, NOT A SKIN WITH A FACE. It exists because a groove is a feature of a surface and there was none: the four clefts hung in space with the pharyngeal wall ending at 0.80 of an intersegment and the clefts beginning at 3.94. It is a thick-walled swept shell because every gate in this model's harness — watertight edge pairing, and the ray-parity test — is defined on a closed solid and an open panel has neither. It carries no surface detail, no facial or limb form and no cervical sinus as a separate structure; it is the body surface as a smooth envelope of the pharyngeal region, and nothing more should be read off its shape.

THE SURFACE ECTODERM TAKES 61% OF BEAT 1's FRAME, MEASURED, AND THAT IS THE COST OF FIXING F4. With the beat's own CROSS_SECTION applied the shares are surface_ectoderm 61.00, pharyngeal_wall 13.71, pouch1 5.21, pouch2 2.06, pouch3 1.90, clefts_lower 1.82, arch_bars 1.11, cleft1 0.92, pouch4 0.79 — every one above the 0.3% floor the corpus uses, but the skin is the backdrop and the apparatus is small in front of it. It is drawn at opacity 0.16 and the player refits the camera to what is visible, so showing the surface enlarges beat 1's frame and shrinks its subject. The alternative considered and NOT taken was a ninth beat carrying the arrangement on its own, which would be the better composition; it was not taken because inserting a beat renumbers every beat after it and every claim id that names one, and this run would rather hand a reviewer a measured trade-off than an unreviewed renumbering. THIS IS THE FIRST THING TO LOOK AT.

BEAT 7's CROSS_SECTION WAS REMOVED THIS RUN BECAUSE IT DELETED THE WHOLE THYROID. The gap note above about CROSS_SECTION cutting only context structures was already in this file and was right; what nobody had done was apply it to beat 7, whose ONE context structure is the thyroid gland. The plane for axis z at offset 0 keeps z <= 0 and the thyroid sits entirely at z 0.51 to 1.39 intersegments ventral, so all of it was clipped: measured 0.000% of the frame, in a beat whose narration says the ultimopharyngeal body is absorbed INTO the thyroid and whose claim B7-dispersed asserts the C cells are inside it. The section is not re-aimed because the authored offset is multiplied by 3 and applied in world space while the model grows 5.6-fold across t, so no fixed offset tracks the gland. It was not needed: the thyroid is drawn at opacity 0.22, which is what lets a student see the cells inside it. Found by render-pharyngeal-pouches.mjs section 12.

THE SCENE INDEX WAS NOT REBUILT AND surface_ectoderm's SEARCH TERMS ARE THEREFORE NOT IN IT. viz-training/scenes/index.json is built by tools/build-scene-index.mjs, which readdirSync's the whole scenes directory and rewrites the file wholesale. This run works on a staged copy of the repo, and while it was running another build run was actively rewriting embryology__pharyngeal-apparatus__pharyngeal-clefts-membranes.json — its mtime moved from the August version to 2026-10-03T18:56 and its size from 29,446 to 82,320 bytes mid-run. Regenerating index.json from this run's snapshot would have written that run's half-finished scene into the shared index, and index.json has no compare-and-swap protection finer than its own mtime. The consequence of leaving it is small and bounded: role 'context' structures do not enter the index's parts list at all, so only the term mappings 'surface ectoderm', 'body surface', 'skin', 'cervical sinus' and 'branchial cyst' are missing, and this scene's structure count reads 22 rather than 23. A corpus-wide run should rebuild it.

THE GROOVES ARE SWEPT AT ring 14 AND LOOK FACETED CLOSE UP. Visible in the beat-4 frame as a sawtooth along the first cleft's upper edge. It is a tessellation choice inherited from before this run and not a winding fault — the harness reads 0 of 1288 hull triangles mis-wound and 0 unpaired edges on cleft1 at every sampled day. Raising the ring count is cheap and was not done because it changes triangle counts, which acceptance row T-poles pins deliberately.

deferred_beats.title: The four-line summary
deferred_beats.narration: Reduce it to four lines and rebuild the detail from them. One, the ear — middle ear cavity and auditory tube. Two, the tonsil. Three, thymus and inferior parathyroid. Four, superior parathyroid and the C cells. Then add the one thing the list cannot show: the third pouch derivative ends up below the fourth pouch derivative, because the thymus dragged it there.
terms: four superior parathyroid and C cells
deferred_beats.why_not_a_view: It is a revision list, and the picture it would draw is the picture beat 3 already draws. RENDER-STANDARD: "A VIEW MUST CHANGE THE PICTURE. If a beat renders the same frame as the one before it — same structures, no highlight, no rotation, no section — it is not a view. It is text, and text has its own home in this app." Every fact in these four lines is made visible somewhere else in the scene: the ear in beats 3 and 4, the tonsil in beat 3, the thymus and the inferior parathyroid in beats 5 and 6, the superior parathyroid and the C cells in beats 6 and 7, and the crossover — the one thing the list cannot show — in beat 6, where it is measured on the beat’s own screen plane. The words are kept here in full and belong in a text panel or a revision card, not in a ninth frame identical to the third.
deferred_beats.where_it_belongs: a text panel at the end of the scene, or the topic’s revision card

visibility_waivers.why: NOT SHOWN RATHER THAN NOT VISIBLE, and the reason is the biology. Beat 7 stands at day 48 because that is the one stage at which the ultimopharyngeal body is half gone and the C cells are half arrived — the handover the narration describes. By day 48 the fourth pouch is at 0.16 of its own peak and its ventral wing at 0.26: both have involuted, which is correct, and drawing them beside the thing they became would show a student two structures that no longer exist. Measured: pouch4 peaks at day 38, the wing at day 40.
visibility_waivers.shown_instead_by: beat 2, at day 38, where every wing is at full extension and a SHOW_RELATIONSHIP runs from pouch4_ventral_wing to ultimopharyngeal_body

visibility_waivers.why: As pouch4 above — 0.26 of its own peak at day 48.

Beat 3 runs down the whole series and its narration names the membrane, but the membrane sits 2.9 intersegments lateral of the pharyngeal axis while the rest of this beat’s subject is within 1.5 — showing it stretched the subject box and took the beat from 9.7% of the frame to 7.2%, under the tool’s 8% subject floor. It is not that the membrane cannot be seen; it is that showing it here makes everything else too small to read.
visibility_waivers.shown_instead_by: beat 4, whose entire subject it is, at 0.93 of an intersegment of screen height

visibility_waivers.why: Beat 3’s narration runs the full series — ear, tonsil, thymus, both parathyroids — and no single camera can hold the ear and the mediastinum at a size a student can read. Measured when it was tried: the subject spanned 179 world units, and the thymus, both parathyroids and the thyroid all drew ZERO pixels because the frame that fits the whole apparatus leaves them a handful of pixels each and the compare op refit the camera onto the pharynx. The beat now shows the first two pouches and the tonsil, which are what a frame this tight can carry, and the words still run the series.
visibility_waivers.shown_instead_by: beats 5 and 6 for the thymus, beat 6 for both parathyroid pairs
beat 6, where the crossover is measured on that beat’s own screen plane

visibility_waivers.why: NOT A WAIVER FOR A STRUCTURE THAT CANNOT BE SEEN — the opposite, and it is recorded here because the number is surprising and a reviewer should meet it with the argument rather than derive it. surface_ectoderm is the NEAREST surface over 61.00% of beat 1's frame once the beat's own CROSS_SECTION is applied. It is context at opacity 0.16, it is the outermost thing the model builds, and the beat is sectioned and seen from `anterior` — so a student is looking into a cut neck with the dorsal half of the skin behind everything. The structures in front of it all clear the 0.3% floor (pouch1 5.21, arch_bars 1.11, cleft1 0.92, pouch4 0.79). The corpus walk, tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs, does NOT implement CROSS_SECTION, so its own numbers for this beat are measured on an uncut shell that covers everything and reports every other structure only through the alpha-aware pass. Both sets of numbers are in BUILD-LOG.md.

BEAT 4 FAILS tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs's 8% SUBJECT-FILL FLOOR, AT 7.71%, AND THIS RUN DID NOT TUNE IT UP. Stated plainly because it is the one corpus check this item does not pass. The beat shows exactly three things — pouch1, the tympanic membrane and cleft1 — so nothing foreign is taking the frame: the subject's own bounding box fills 31.4% and its ink is 7.71%, because the tubotympanic recess is a long tapering cone lying diagonally and a diagonal cone fills about a quarter of its own box. It measured 8.41% before this run only because the tympanic membrane was drawn 1.7 times the width of the recess it caps — an overhanging saucer, visible as one in the render — and the overhang was ink. Sizing it honestly at 1.15 of the tip calibre cost 0.70 of a percentage point. WHAT WAS TRIED: widening the membrane to 1.40 of the tip calibre, which is still a rim rather than a saucer and still defensible anatomically, reached 7.99% — one hundredth of a point short. That is the signal that the membrane's width is not what this measure is about, so it was put back to 1.15, which is the size chosen for the picture rather than for the threshold. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT is a camera perpendicular to the recess's own axis, which is neither of the two the player offers near it (`lateral` gives the membrane first-hit 0.5429 and `anterior` 0.3786), or splitting the beat so the calibre claim keeps the whole cone and the apposition claim gets a close view of the tip. Both are composition changes a review should weigh, not a builder's to make unilaterally in a rework round.
